ProTip, Since I would guess, as an editor, you likely have multiple displays (if you don't, get a second one, NOW, its SO helpful), make them different. IPS is great for color accuracy, but you do have to remember that the bulk of your viewers will be watching on TN, though that number will be falling. As such, there's no harm in seeing how it looks on each. When I've made stuff in premiere, ae, and photoshop (i'm just a tinkerer in the adobe space, mainly work as a hobby in 3d via maya, mudbox, and zbrush), I've actually checked previews on different displays. The other suggestion I would have would be to go to your local photography shop, and rent a colorimeter to calibrate your display(s). The change is phenomenal. ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS err on the side of too bright, since a good number of displays are configured out of the box for 'movie mode,' which crushes every grey and brown that's even vaguely dark into pitch black.
